stories.title: Rep. Josh Gottheimer sells Applied Materials and McDonald's shares
stories.summary: A new disclosure shows Rep. Josh Gottheimer sold stock in Applied Materials and McDonald's. The filing does not give the trade size or the sale price. Investing.com reported the disclosure on October 9.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors track congressional stock trades for early signals on sector views, even when lawmakers say the trades follow routine rules.
whatToWatch: The full disclosure filing for trade size and date
Any pattern in Gottheimer's other recent trades
questions: What was the size of each trade?
What prompted the timing of the sale?

stories.title: Relay Therapeutics CEO sells $872,401 in company stock
stories.summary: Relay Therapeutics CEO Sanjiv Patel sold $872,401 worth of company shares, according to an insider filing reported by Investing.com. The filing does not state the reason for the sale.
stories.whyItMatters: Insider sales draw scrutiny, though they often follow a preset trading plan rather than a change in outlook.
whatToWatch: Whether the sale was part of a scheduled trading plan
Future insider filings from Relay Therapeutics executives
questions: Was this sale part of a 10b5-1 trading plan?
Does the sale reflect a change in the CEO's view of the stock?

stories.title: Nvidia-backed AI data centre operator Firmus scraps $5 billion IPO
stories.summary: Firmus, an Australian AI data centre operator backed by Nvidia, has scrapped its planned $5 billion IPO, according to Investing.com. The report does not give the reason behind the decision.
stories.whyItMatters: A pulled IPO from an AI infrastructure firm raises questions about investor appetite for data centre valuations despite strong demand for AI computing capacity.
whatToWatch: Whether Firmus pursues a smaller listing or private funding instead
Reaction from other AI infrastructure firms weighing public listings
questions: Why did Firmus scrap the IPO?
Will Firmus seek funding through other channels?

stories.title: Starbucks declines to comment on Chipotle takeover report

Starbucks' next earnings update on turnaround progress
questions: Is any deal discussion actually underway?

stories.title: Pharvaris HAE drug shows faster symptom relief in Lancet study
stories.summary: A study published in The Lancet found that Pharvaris's hereditary angioedema drug gave patients faster symptom relief, according to Investing.com. The report does not give further trial detail.
stories.whyItMatters: Positive trial data can shape Pharvaris's regulatory path and its competitive position in the hereditary angioedema drug market.
whatToWatch: Further trial results or data readouts
questions: How does the drug's speed of relief compare with existing HAE treatments?
When might Pharvaris seek regulatory approval based on this data?
